rnd_001: You can recognise it by seeing only its crown from the track above, walking down to the streamside bank to find the full trunk. It stands at Cuesta de la Laja, Sierra de las Nieves.
rnd_002: You can recognise it by its candelabrum shape, forking low into two and then three trunks instead of one straight spire. It stands above the Puerto de La Perra.
rnd_003: You can recognise it by being hidden among firs on bare, steep, thin-soiled ground with almost no shrub layer around it. It stands at Froncaile, Sierra de las Nieves.
rnd_004: You can recognise it by its enormous trunk, 14.65 metres round, and two huge main limbs, with a stone wall built behind it against erosion. It stands at Hoyo del Bote.
rnd_005: You can recognise it by standing right at the trackside where the slope begins to fall away toward the stream, impossible to walk past. It stands on the Camino del Molino Real.
rnd_006: You can recognise it as the only tree in sight, its base spread wide over the bare rock it grows on. It stands on a crag near the Puerto del Pinsapo.
